LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 6.3.1 FICTION: ANTHOLOGY OF SHORT STORIES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Fiction and Non- Fiction 6.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- Fiction 6.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How has history and culture influenced the short story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the features of a short story for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 6.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. interpret the elements of culture in the short story for lifelong learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 6.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate aspects of Kenyan history to the short story for critical analysis, ● Learners with low vision search for features of short stories from Kenya from online and offline sources and present findings to the class while learners with blindness search for features of short stories from Kenya from braille media or digital devices and present findings to the class, How has history and culture influenced the short story? 54 - Short stories and the culture of Kenya

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non- Fiction 6.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate how history and culture have shaped the short story as a form of fiction. ● In groups learners with low vision and learners with blindness collaborate to discuss the features of the short stories and peer review, pick out elements of culture in the short stories, ● Learners with low vision and learners with blindness team up to identify elements of Kenyan history from the short stories, ● Learners with low vision summarise findings using graphic organisers, while learners with blindness summarise their work in braille ● Learners relate the events of a short story to the history and culture of Kenya, ● Learners with low vision and learners with blindness team up to collect short stories from Kenya and organise them in a class portfolio, 55 ● Learners conduct a reading session on the short stories collected and review with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- Fiction 6.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: This is nurtured as the learner collaborates and uses their imagination to summarise their

findings using graphic organisers.

● Digital literacy: This is developed as the learner interacts with digital content when searching for features of short

stories from Kenya from online and offline sources.

Values:
● Social justice: This is inculcated as the learner appreciates the contributions of the others during discussions and peer

reviews.

● Unity: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to collect short stories from Kenya and organise in a

class portfolio.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner observes equity and non- discrimination while identifying elements of Kenyan

history from the short stories.
